newsitem.title: USA: GM plans flat Q2 N. American production.
newsitem.headline: GM plans flat Q2 N. American production.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Thursday it plans to build 1,550,000 cars and trucks in North America during the second quarter, about flat with the 1,549,000 it produced during the same period of 1996.

But GM said it increased its first quarter production estimates to 1,438,000 total vehicles for the United States, Canada and Mexico, an increase of about 7,000 units from estimates released a month ago.

GM said it increased estimated first quarter North American passenger car production by 12,000 units and decreased truck production by 5,000 units. The company attibuted the car increase to the successful production launch of 14 new products for the 1997 model year.
The first quarter production total is 18 percent higher than the company's first quarter 1996 output and calls for 788,000 cars and 650,000 trucks.

In the second quarter, GM said it plans to build 850,000 cars and 700,000 trucks in North America -- representing GM's highest quarter ever for truck production. In the second quarter of 1996, GM built 894,000 cars and 655,000 cars in North America.

GM also said it built 491,000 total vehicles in February in North America, a 1.2 percent decrease from the 497,000 vehicles built in February 1996. The February 1997 total includes 266,000 cars and 225,000 trucks, compared with 288,000 cars and 209,000 cars and trucks in the year-ago period.
